text:
Going from Tokyo to Lake Kawaguchi?
Don't count on the direct train after lunch.
On December weekdays, the last regular one
leaves Shinjuku at 10:30 👇

🗺️ Route and map 👉 https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-to-kawaguchiko-big-suitcase-bus-or-train

❌ The mistake
You enjoy a slow morning in Tokyo.
Then you look for the direct train at noon.
But on weekdays there are only four:
7:30, 8:30, 9:30 and 10:30.
(Plus a seasonal 11:34 until 29 December.)
Every seat is reserved, on sale a month ahead.
At weekends, they're often gone.

✅ The fix
1️⃣ Leaving after 10:30?
Take the Kaiji limited express from Shinjuku.
It leaves at about half past each hour
and reaches Otsuki in about an hour.

2️⃣ At Otsuki, stay inside the station.
Walk through the transfer gate
to the Fujikyu platform.

3️⃣ Fujikyu trains leave 1 to 3 times an hour.
Example: the 12:30 Kaiji meets the 13:55 local.
Otsuki to Kawaguchiko is ¥1,170.
No seat ticket needed on the local.

4️⃣ Running late?
The last weekday link is the 21:59 Kaiji.
It meets the 23:10 last train.

🚌 Or take the bus from Busta Shinjuku.
It runs until 22:25 and costs ¥2,000 online.
One big suitcase per person rides free.

💡 Direct train showing no seats left?
There's a ticket without a seat number.
It's on the railway's own page, and in our guide.

👉 Both routes, step by step:
https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-to-kawaguchiko-big-suitcase-bus-or-train
